page: Google Cloud Platform c2d-highcpu-2 is a compute-optimized virtual machine instance based on the x86_64 architecture. It features 2 vCPUs mapped to 1 physical core of an AMD EPYC 7B13 processor, supporting 2 threads per core with dedicated CPU allocation. The instance is configured with 4.0 GB of system memory, yielding 2.0 GB of RAM per core. It does not include bundled local storage or GPU accelerators, and provides zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark evaluations reveal a distinct performance profile. The instance demonstrates strong single-core CPU performance in stress-ng tests, placing in the top 25%. However, multi-core CPU performance and overall PassMark CPU scores fall into the bottom 25%. Memory performance is a notable bottleneck, with cached small-block read bandwidth and overall PassMark memory scores ranking in the bottom 10%. Single-threaded gzip compression and bzip3 decompression show average performance, while database operations and Redis SET throughput are weak, landing in the bottom 10%.

This instance represents a low-resource entry point for dedicated AMD EPYC compute power. While it offers cost-efficient access to dedicated CPU execution, the low memory capacity of 4.0 GB and constrained memory bandwidth limit its utility for memory-intensive applications. It is best suited for lightweight, single-threaded compute tasks, basic text processing, or small-scale web serving where multi-core scaling and high memory throughput are not critical.
